recorded.DefaultEncodingIsLocale: This example starts other Python programs (child interpreters) to show the encoding under different locale settings, which a browser cannot do, so it is not run on this page.
recorded.SerializationErrorNotes: The notes that Python 3.14 attaches to a JSON error (which list item or dictionary key failed) do not exist in Python 3.13, which is the Python of this page, so the example would print without them; it is not run on this page.

notice: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with xmltodict 1.0.4, defusedxml 0.7.1 and openpyxl 3.1.5 (the versions the chapter was recorded with, embedded as wheels) on Pyodide's own lxml 6.0.0; the recording ran under Python 3.14.6 with lxml 6.1.3. Each example was checked in the browser against its recorded result. Two examples need something a browser cannot give (other Python programs with other locale settings, and the notes of Python 3.14's JSON errors) and are shown as recorded, not run. Not executed at all: Microsoft Excel itself (LibreOffice stood in for it), a real Windows computer (the line-end translation of Windows text mode was reproduced with io.TextIOWrapper and is called EMULATED where it is shown), Python 3.14.7, 3.14.8 and the final 3.15.0, and the language-model clean-up. Memory and time figures are MEASURED once, on one machine, and are single runs, not results of the program.
